Assessment with SLOOS overlay:
- FOMC communication: Holds the funds rate at 1–1.25% with guidance for “gradual increases” and begins balance sheet normalization in October—signals a mild tightening bias, consistent with interest-rate smoothing. Inflation remains below 2% with a symmetric target; hurricane-related spikes viewed as transitory.
- SLOOS signals (July 2017): Domestic banks report weaker demand for CRE (construction, land development, multifamily) and for consumer credit (auto, credit card), with tighter standards for consumer loans; residential mortgage standards generally eased/unchanged. Foreign banks report tighter standards for C&I (across firm sizes) and CRE, with some strengthening in CRE loan demand.
- Policy implications: The soft demand and tighter standards in consumer and parts of CRE suggest marginal headwinds to credit growth that temper the hawkishness implied by balance sheet runoff and “gradual” hikes. Net tone remains slightly hawkish but closer to neutral when incorporating SLOOS.
